_README: SDI's prices, as DATA — reviewable and changeable without a code edit.
Every entry is one price. `amount` is the money; everything beside it is what an
estimator needs to decide whether to trust it: where it came from, when that source
was current, what it may price, how firm it is, and when it should be looked at again.
status:  live       a current system/supplier price — the engine may charge it
confirmed  a current quote or figure confirmed for its scope
historical a dated quote from an earlier job — priced only as a LABELLED
comparator, never as a silent default
indicative a market/derived figure — priced, labelled, to be replaced
scope:   material / department / customer / job_family / job_only. `job_only` prices
that job and nothing else; it is written here only for the audit trail, and
the job's own answers file remains where such a figure belongs.
review_date is not decoration. Past it, the engine keeps pricing — silence is worse —
and says the figure is out of review so nobody mistakes age for agreement.
historical_audit_record is OUTSIDE the resolver. load() does not read it, lookup()
cannot return it, and no estimate can charge, display or fall back to it. It exists so a
figure somebody once quoted is not lost to the audit trail — and for nothing else.

historical_audit_record.label: Brass — Harrods 01 decorative plating
historical_audit_record.source_reference: plater quote via SDI estimating (Howard Thurley), job 7332-01
historical_audit_record.notes: Kept for audit and NOT for pricing. James Gray, 16 Sep 2026: a new estimate must be independent of an earlier one — this figure may not appear as a charge, a fallback, a comparator, a workbook note or a suggested value. What 7332-01 taught is that Harrods 01 is DECORATIVE plating, so the per-kg zinc card cannot price it and a fresh job-specific quote is required. That knowledge lives in config.NAMED_PLATE_SPECS; this number lives here and goes nowhere.
